grandparents_cupboard.reason: Flour, butter, cheddar, egg, milk, mustard and cabbage are all ordinary home staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday, cheap Tesco item.

basic_kitchen.reason: Rubbed-in scones need only a frying pan, bowl and baking tray, which is well within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: The 300g flour, 60g butter and roughly 175ml of egg and milk give a standard soft scone dough. Eight wedges suit four people as a snack, and 20 minutes at 220°C is right for a thick round.

honest_times.reason: Shredding, frying for 5 minutes, grating, rubbing in and shaping fit in 20 active minutes, and the 20-minute bake matches the step.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the thyme, mustard and pepper, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used.

seasonal_feel.reason: Warm cheese scones suit late December, and 150g of Savoy folded through makes the cabbage a real part of the bake.

plain_voice.reason: The steps read as plain, friendly British instructions, and "pat into a 3cm round" is the usual shorthand for thickness.

hearty_healthy.reason: Cheese, egg and a good amount of cabbage make this a proper, satisfying snack that a family would bake again.
